issues.legal_issue: A prior possessor who has not proved ownership may recover possession from a wrongdoer on the strength of possessory title, even when the action is brought more than six months after dispossession.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s ownership of the land was not proved.
The evidence established that the plaintiff possessed the land from about 1930 until about 1945, when the second defendant trespassed and took possession.
The suit for possession was instituted in 1949, more than six months after the dispossession.
The defendants’ claim of title by adverse possession was not established.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff’s prior possession gave him a sufficient title against the defendants, who had not established that they were lawful owners. The decree for possession was upheld and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, the summary remedy is distinct from an ordinary action of ejectment: prior possession is sufficient title against a wrongdoer even when the ejectment action is brought more than six months after dispossession. A trespasser cannot defeat the prior possessor by asserting that title and the right to possession belong to a third person. The Court applied Ismail Ariff v. Mohamed Ghouse and approved Narayana Row v. Dharmachar, Krishnarav Yashvant v. Vasudev Apaji Ghotikar, Singh v. Ramji Das, Wali Ahmad Khan v. Ajudhia Khandu, and Subodh Gopal Bose v. Province of Bihar; it held that the contrary Calcutta decisions in Debi Churn Boldo v. Issur Chunder Manjee, Ertaza Hossein v. Bany Mistry, Purmeshur Chowdhry v. Brijo Lal Chowdhry, and Nisa Chand Gaita v. Kanchiram Bagani did not state the law correctly.

rule.if: ejectment_action and plaintiff_prior_possession and defendant_wrongdoer and not defendant_lawful_title_established

predicates.ejectment_action: The claimant brought an ordinary action seeking recovery of possession from the person in possession.
predicates.plaintiff_prior_possession: The claimant had possession of the property before being dispossessed.
predicates.defendant_wrongdoer: The person in possession took or retained the property by wrongful dispossession rather than under an established lawful right.
predicates.defendant_lawful_title_established: The person in possession established a lawful title or right to possess the property.
predicates.plaintiff_entitled_to_possession: The claimant is entitled to recover possession of the property.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeking possession in an ordinary ejectment action proves prior possession and the opposing possessor is a wrongdoer who has not established lawful title, the claimant is entitled to possession.
